changes: Add four explicit mutable-donor resize policies for bounded/count and packed/preserved-row-column operations without requiring Clone.
Move old receiver storage into a temporary before default construction; publish the new initialized rectangle before assignment callbacks.
Retain native partial destination values and new bounds after assignment failure, then destroy owned old elements in order; borrowed old donors remain mutated in external storage.
Share the phase engine with existing Clone convenience methods using a private read-only donor adapter, preserving Shared views without extra detachment or Clone constructor calls.
Correct same-dimension copy=true resizing to rebase only, preserving an independently changed inherited Array1 length exactly as the native branch does.
Extract Array1 no-copy resizing without Clone restrictions; keep its existing Vec initialization and replacement behavior.
probe_policy: The native payload records Default, copy/move assignment, copy construction and destruction events. Rust payloads retain injected Rc recorders; a guard installs the recorder only for parameterless Default on each independent test thread. The assignment callbacks use explicit mutable donor operations; the convenience policy is joined to a native copy-assignment fallback class.
limitations: Explicit assignment closures model the selected native element move/copy assignment; Rust traits do not automatically infer arbitrary C++ element operation policies.

Constructor failure receiver state is observed for a failure at the first default. Native resizeImpl leaks its newly allocated buffer on constructor failure, while Rust Vec safely reclaims it. Later partial-construction cleanup and native allocation accounting remain unported domains.

Trivially default-constructible C++ elements may remain uninitialized, while ordinary Rust T: Default creates initialized values. Native Array1 trivial reallocation policy and allocation hooks are not proved.

Explicit mutable-donor operations detach safe Shared views before mutable donor access. Native arbitrary writable/const-cast aliases, callback reentry, and retained pointers across exclusive borrows remain outside this interface.

Rust checked extent/overflow behavior outside native-defined integer arithmetic is an extension, not a parity claim. No guarantee is made for panicking Drop where native destruction terminates or differs.
The public representation of Array1/Array2 is unchanged; Send/Sync/Unpin and outer storage lifetime covariance compile checks are included. No universal ABI or trait equivalence is claimed.
Original assertions are unchanged. These scoped bindings do not declare either array class complete and add no global inventory or original-declaration credit.
